newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BNDES sees CVRD voting stake sold above base price.
newsitem.headline: BNDES sees CVRD voting stake sold above base price.

text.p: The vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) expects a 45 percent voting stake in Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) to be sold 10 to 15 percent above its base price, newspapers said.
The minimum price of the 45 percent stake which will be auctioned off on April 29 was set at 3.0 billion reais.
Jose Pio Borges told O Globo newspaper he expects a third consortium will be formed to compete with the groups being built by Brazilian cement group Grupo Votorantim and steelmaker CSN.
This new consortium would include Australian mining firms, Brazilian mining firm Caemi and some investors already in talks with Votorantim and CSN, Pio Borges told the paper.

Grupo Votorantim is teaming up with Japan's Nippon Steel, South Africa's Anglo-American and other investors, while CSN is trying to form a consortium with local construction group Camargo Correa, pulp and paper group Suzano, Japan's Mitsui, Banco Opportunity and George Soros and Nations Bank funds, the newspaper said.
